meta.title: Download ai-memory and read the changelog
meta.description: Download ai-memory {tag} for Linux, macOS and Windows, or install it with mise, the AUR or Docker. Checksums, release history and the full changelog.

hero.title: Download ai-memory {tag}
hero.lede: Released {date}. One self-contained binary per platform, each with a SHA-256 checksum next to it. MIT licensed.

builds.title: Binaries
builds.after: After unpacking, follow the quick setup. On Linux and macOS, install.sh and ai-memory setup do it in two commands.

mac.note: Includes a launchd agent. If you download with a browser, clear the quarantine flag first.

win.note: Experimental. WSL2 with the Linux build is the supported path.

builds.upgrade: Later, a binary under a writable prefix (Linux, macOS, the Windows zip) updates itself with ai-memory upgrade: it downloads the matching release, verifies the checksum and refreshes the hooks. Packages update through their package manager.

channels.title: Package managers and containers

mise.title: mise
mise.note: Linux and macOS. Verifies the checksum for you. New releases can take about a day to appear.

aur.title: Arch Linux (AUR)
aur.note: Installs systemd units for a user or a system service.

rpm.title: Fedora (RPM)
rpm.note: x86_64 and aarch64 packages with the binary, the hook sources and the systemd units. Then follow the user or system service steps.

docker.title: Docker or Podman
docker.note: Multi-arch: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so Apple Silicon needs no emulation.

src.title: From source
src.note: Needs the Rust toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml.

channels.clients: Client machines that only send hooks to a remote server do not need the full binary. The release also ships ai-memory-install-hooks and wrapper scripts for Docker on Linux, macOS and Windows. They are listed on the release page.

changelog.title: What changed
changelog.lede: A short summary of the newest release, then the counts for the ones before it. The full changelog on GitHub has every entry.
changelog.stale: The summary for {tag} is being written. The counts below cover it, and the full changelog has every entry.

highlights.title: Search finds the right session far more often
highlights.text: A session page keeps only an excerpt of each turn, so the answer often lived only in the raw observations. They now vote in ranking. On LongMemEval-S, hit@5 went from 0.82 to 0.95 with the default install, with no LLM. One config flag restores the old ranking.

highlights.title: Two commands to install
highlights.text: install.sh downloads the release, verifies the checksum and links the binary with no root. ai-memory setup creates the data directory, starts a per-user service and wires every agent it finds. Claude Code and Codex can use a marketplace plugin instead.

highlights.title: A token by default
highlights.text: A fresh install mints a bearer token into an owner-only file that the hooks, the CLI and the MCP bridge read. Older installs keep working and switch with ai-memory auth enable. The 1.x token commands are gone; tokens they issued keep working as API keys.

highlights.title: The web UI grew up
highlights.text: Page history with a diff between any two versions, a session timeline you can replay, backlinks and an outline on every page, a search that ranks like the agent’s with an explain mode, mail badges, a health page for root, and a sign-in. Still read-only.

highlights.title: More agents
highlights.text: Factory Droid and Meta Muse Code with full hooks, GitHub Copilot CLI through the launcher, Prime Agent and DeepSeek Harness over MCP, written recipes for six more clients, and a Cursor subscription as an LLM provider.

highlights.title: Recovery and sync
highlights.text: ai-memory recover replays what hooks spooled while the server was down. Page writes can carry a precondition so two writers never clobber each other, which the team-wiki sync and a new importer build on. A TypeScript SDK covers programs that are not coding agents.
